assumptions: out_SB r1 is one SB travel lane (its left ~3.5 m) plus a kerbside parking strip; the left turn is received only by the travel-lane part.
The left-turning traffic comes from in_WB r1 alone. No left-turn arrow or ONLY marking was read in r2.
movements.reason: in_WB r1 is the lane beside the raised median. The satellite (spring 2021) shows two left-curving arrows in it. The mid street view (2020-11) shows the same lane, bounded by the median kerb and a solid white line, with 'ONLY' and a wide turn arrow ahead; the satellite shapes fix that arrow as left. In the full scene the south leg leaves the junction to the WB driver's left (south-west), and out_SB r1 is the only supported SB motor region there. The pair is therefore in_WB r1 to out_SB r1. The far view (104 m) shows one wide lane, with a new lane line starting downstream, so r1 is a left-turn pocket rather than a continuation of a through lane.

assumptions: out_WB has a single motor receiving lane (r1, about 4.6-5 m, no internal lane line). Its r2 is a hatched buffer and r3 a buffered bicycle lane, so neither receives motor traffic.
in_WB r3 (kerbside bicycle strip) is not a motor endpoint.
movements.reason: in_WB r2 carries straight-ahead arrows in the satellite, near the stop bar and upstream, and a compact straight arrow in the camera lane of the mid street view. It sits between the solid line shared with the ONLY lane and the solid line beside the bicycle strip. Across the junction the WB carriageway continues north-west with one wide travel lane (out_WB r1), between a median island kerb and a hatched buffer. So the through lane maps one-to-one to out_WB r1. r1 does not feed through, because its arrows are left-turn and it carries ONLY. Confidence is medium, not high, because the satellite arrows lie in building shadow and the near view (2020-11) shows freshly resurfaced, unmarked pavement at the stop line.

assumptions: If a U-turn were made, it would start from the median-side lane in_WB r1 and enter out_EB r2, the EB travel lane beside the median (out_EB r1 is the median itself).
movements.reason: No U-turn arrow, U-turn sign or U-turn prohibition sign is visible in any view. The r1 arrows read as left-turn shapes without a U-turn hook, though they are low-resolution and shadowed. A raised median separates the carriageways. The junction is wide enough that the path is geometrically conceivable, but whether it is legal cannot be seen, so the movement is left unresolved. The listed pair is only the geometric hypothesis.

gsv_alignment_notes: Mid view (55.6 m, 2020-11) binds by physical order from the median kerb: ONLY/left lane = in_WB r1, straight-arrow camera lane = r2, kerbside strip to the granite kerb = r3. This order matches the satellite regions.
Far view (103.8 m) shows a single wide general lane plus a kerbside strip. The lane line that creates r1 starts downstream of it, so r1 has no counterpart there: it is a turn pocket.

Near view (23.5 m) shows freshly resurfaced black asphalt without lane lines or arrows at capture time, so it gives no lane-use evidence. Its green kerbside strip supports r3 as a bicycle facility. The 2021 satellite arrows postdate that resurfacing and agree with the mid view.

out_WB and out_EB were read from a reverse look-back panorama of the opposing approach. They were matched by physical sequence (median, travel lane, buffer, bike lane or parking), not by lane ordinal.
There is no motor leg on the north side (only a path between a building and a park), consistent with no right-turn movement being requested for WB.
